    • blankLookingCharacterIn

      public static String blankLookingCharacterIn(String text)
      Describes the first character of the text that the eye reads as a blank but the parser does not: a no-break space, a narrow one, a zero-width one.

      They arrive by copying out of a word processor, a web page or a chat window; they survive String.trim(), which only removes characters up to U+0020; and they are invisible in every editor. A value that fails over one therefore gives the reader nothing whatever to look at, which is why it is worth naming the character rather than only reporting that the value was refused.

      Parameters:
      text - the text to examine.
      Returns:
      a description naming the character and where it sits, or null if there is none.

    • splitNumericAndChar

      public static String[] splitNumericAndChar(String input)
      Splits a string into a numeric part and a character part. The input string should conform to the format [numeric_part][char_part] with an optional whitespace between the two parts. The char_part should only contain letters as defined by Character.isLetter(char) while the numeric_part will be parsed regardless of content. Any whitespace will be trimmed from the beginning and end of both parts, however, the numeric_part can contain whitespaces within it.
      Parameters:
      input - the string to split.
      Returns:
      an array of two strings.

    • hideCredentials

      public static String hideCredentials(URI uri)
      The text of a source, with any credentials in it replaced.

      A URI may carry them — https://user:secret@config/app.properties is legal and used — and the source is exactly what a message about a source has to name. The rule that a value never reaches a log does not cover this, the secret being in the source rather than in a value, so it is covered here instead: everything between the scheme and the host becomes ***.

      Parameters:
      uri - the source, may be null.
      Returns:
      the source as text, with no credentials in it.

    • newInstance

      public static <T> T newInstance(Class<T> clazz)
      Instantiates the given class using its no-argument constructor, whatever its visibility and whatever the visibility of the class itself.

      A Preprocessor, a Converter, a Tokenizer or a decryptor is an implementation detail of the configuration that names it, and until 2.0.0 all four had to be public — which meant a library using OWNER had to widen its own API to satisfy ours. The class was not being asked to be visible to us, which would be fair: it was being asked to be visible to everybody, since this method lives in a package of its own and "the same package" is therefore never true of anyone else's code. Even a package-private class next to the interface that named it was refused.

      The access check is lifted for the length of the call. Where it cannot be — a security manager that says no, or a module that does not open the package — the constructor is called as it is and the refusal that follows is the one that was raised before.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the instance.
      Parameters:
      clazz - the class to instantiate.
      Returns:
      a new instance of the given class.
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the class cannot be instantiated.
